lines.text: Boarding pass? Sorted. Lounge access? Let's not find out at the desk. I'm Pip. Tell me your exact card and when you're flying. I'll check the bank's conditions, and show you where I found them.

No spending last quarter? Wait, don't walk away yet. This reviewed I C I C I savings policy has a balance route too. Our example has twelve lakh rupees in qualifying deposits, so that condition passes. The exact lounge is still unverified. We keep that question open.

Hang on. Twelve visits a year, or three a quarter? These H D F C pages have different dates. The July twenty twenty six terms require sixty thousand rupees in eligible spending, with three visits per quarter. The older headline doesn't settle this trip. A possible new card exception still needs confirmation.

Delhi. Terminal three. Domestic. Now we're getting somewhere. For this October tenth Axis trip, count July, August and September. The example meets the spending rule and has two quarterly visits left. There's Encalm in the reviewed directory. Table three, page four, row twenty three. That's the match we needed.

Want to see my working? The bank documents are linked to dated policies in Sanity. The live agent reads that Knowledge Base before answering. Those two ticks are completed Context calls. Open the sources and check the wording yourself. You don't have to take my word for it.

We checked thirty eight live policy cases, forty five automated tests, and four live agent scenarios. The documents are real; these travellers are made up. I can check the published conditions. The bank and lounge still decide admission. Right, you've got the rule and the source. Keep an eye on your gate too.
Oh, you're early. Good. I'm Pip. Before you join the lounge queue, let's check your card and your trip. Want me to walk you through it?
First, the exact card. World Mastercard and Visa Signature can have different rules, even with the same bank name. Pick the one printed on your card. No card number needed.
Where are we flying? Pick the date, airport, terminal and domestic or international section. A lounge in terminal three doesn't help you in terminal one.
Now the bit that catches people out. Spending has a date window. Use eligible spending for the window shown here, then add visits already used. Not sure of a number? Leave it unknown. We won't guess.
Here's your result. Open Bank evidence to see the original wording, or Ask Pip for the live explanation. If the lounge hasn't been verified, that question stays open.
The published conditions pass for these facts. Good. Now check the lounge match and any remaining questions below. The bank and lounge still decide whether you're admitted.
This trip doesn't meet every published condition. Look at the decision trail below. It shows which check stopped the result. If a fact is wrong, change it and check again.
I can't settle this one yet. See what we still need below. An unknown isn't a rejection. It's a question we should answer before you reach the desk.
Let's try a trip that surprises people. Zero spending, twelve lakh rupees in qualifying deposits. Watch the balance route. Then look at the lounge question separately.
A similar name isn't enough. This pilot has reviewed rules for three card families. If yours isn't covered, I'll say so. Better that than sending you to the wrong queue.
